title: Warehouse Rental Costs in Midrand: Base Rent and Beyond
seoTitle: Warehouse Rental Costs in Midrand | Budget Guide
seoDescription: Build a warehouse occupation budget using a dated Midpoint asking example. Separate base rent, recurring charges and upfront spending before requesting a quote.
excerpt: Calculate indicative warehouse base rent, compare recurring and upfront costs, and request a complete quote for the actual premises.
contentHtml:
Warehouse rental costs in Midrand start with the agreed rentable area and asking rate, then expand into the charges, services and work needed to operate from the premises. Build the budget in three parts: recurring occupation costs, upfront commitments and the costs of running your own operation.

Use this article alongside the Midpoint warehouse leasing guide and current warehouse vacancies. Published figures help you shortlist; a dated quote for the selected unit establishes what is included, excluded and still subject to agreement.

Calculate base rent using the correct area

Where a quote specifies a monthly rate per square metre, multiply that rate by the agreed rentable area. Confirm whether the schedule includes offices, mezzanines or other components, and how yards or exclusive-use areas are charged. Do not add an external yard to the building area unless the quote explicitly uses that basis.

The 6 Weaver Avenue listing, checked on 19 October 2026, publishes 11,443 m² at R109 per m² per month. That gives R1,247,287 per month in indicative base rent: 11,443 × R109. This is arithmetic from the published fields, not an approved total occupation quote. Confirm the area basis, VAT treatment, yard charging and all additional costs with leasing.

Its description separates 10,150 m² of warehousing and 1,293 m² of offices, which add to the published building area. A 5,800 m² yard is described separately. The 6 Weaver listing walkthrough explains the scope and verification questions behind those figures.

Ask for a recurring-cost schedule

Give each cost a description, amount or calculation basis, billing frequency and inclusion status. Where a figure is not confirmed, mark it outstanding rather than entering zero.

  • Premises: base rent, any separately charged yard or ancillary space, and the area to which each rate applies.
  • Property charges: ask whether rates, levies, operating costs or service recoveries are included or billed separately.
  • Usage and services: establish electricity, water, connectivity, waste and any backup-service charging or allocation relevant to the unit.
  • Parking and access: confirm allocated bays, any separate charges, access arrangements and operational restrictions.
  • Changes over time: request the proposed escalation, review dates and how variable charges are calculated.

Keep amounts on the same VAT and monthly basis before comparing quotes. A lower advertised rate does not establish the lower complete cost.

Separate upfront spending from the monthly bill

List the deposit or security requested, fit-out, racking, equipment moves, installations and any work required before occupation. Record who supplies and pays for each item, what approvals are needed and whether the proposed date depends on that work. These are questions for the particular proposal; no standard deposit or landlord contribution is assumed here.

Your own labour, handling equipment, stock systems and transport spending belong in the operating budget alongside the property decision. They are not automatically services supplied by the landlord.

Test whether the space will support the budgeted operation

A quote only becomes useful when its space and service assumptions match your requirements. Use the warehouse specification checklist to check loading, usable clearance, yard circulation and technical capacity. Use the backup-power guide to distinguish a published estate feature from the allocation to your equipment.

Keep Kingfisher outside worked rent examples

2 Kingfisher Avenue remains flagged: its numeric area is 3,849 m², while the description states 3,300 m². Obtain an approved area schedule and reconciled quote before using either figure for a monthly-rent calculation. This article does not resolve that conflict.

Check live availability, then request a warehouse quote and viewing with your area, loading, services, budget and timing brief. Explore the wider Midpoint guides for location, office and estate comparisons.

title: Halfway House vs Waterfall Offices: Compare Your Options
seoTitle: Halfway House vs Waterfall Offices | Midrand
seoDescription: Compare Halfway House and Waterfall offices using the same brief, complete costs, layouts and journey checks. Explore current Midpoint office vacancies.
excerpt: Compare actual office proposals in Halfway House and Waterfall by layout, total cost, services and access, with source-linked location context.
contentHtml:
Compare Halfway House and Waterfall offices using the same workplace brief: the people attending, client visits, usable layout, service requirements and complete cost. Choose between actual buildings and written proposals; the area name alone cannot establish which office will work better for your team.

This comparison supports the Midpoint office leasing guide and location guide. Midpoint is at 162 Tonetti Street, Halfway House, Midrand. Waterfall City is a separate office search area with several distinct precincts and buildings; this article does not represent Waterfall inventory or quote its market rentals.

Make the location comparison specific

For the Halfway House side, use the selected Midpoint unit and the entrance relevant to a viewing. For the Waterfall side, choose an actual building rather than treating the whole city as one office park.

The official Waterfall City CBD guide, checked on 19 October 2026, places its CBD beside the N1 and Allandale Road and lists office destinations including Maxwell Office Park, Nexus Waterfall, the Allandale Building and The Ingress. It describes a mixed-use setting around Mall of Africa. Those location references help define a shortlist; they do not establish a particular suite's availability, package, parking or access rights.

Use one brief for both quotes

Write down daily attendance, private and shared work areas, meeting frequency, confidential work, visitor volumes and storage needs. Add parking requirements, critical equipment, the intended occupation date and any non-negotiable access requirements. Give both leasing contacts the same brief.

Midpoint's 7 Sunbird Road ground-floor listing, checked on 19 October 2026, publishes 500.66 m² at R120 per m² per month. It is one dated Midpoint asking example, not a Halfway House market average or a comparison quote for Waterfall. Confirm the current area schedule, occupation timing, layout and complete charges for this unit.

Compare premises on five practical checks

  • Layout: compare current floor plans, usable work and meeting areas, natural-light positions and the alterations each proposal requires. A larger advertised area is not automatically a better layout.
  • Total cost: align area basis, term and VAT treatment, then separate rent, property recoveries, parking, utilities and fit-out. Identify every unconfirmed item.
  • Services: request unit-specific power, water, connectivity and backup allocations, operating limits and responsible contacts.
  • Access: test staff arrival, client reception, parking and deliveries from the actual entrance at representative times.
  • Working environment: establish which facilities are operating, who may use them, their hours and any booking, membership or usage charges.

The office quote worksheet and floor-plan and fit-out guide help keep those records consistent.

Test journeys without assuming a commute advantage

Map the journeys that matter to your staff and clients, including the final approach, entry procedure and walk to the suite. Record the day, time, route and conditions when checking a journey. Use current transport information for any service your team would depend on.

Neither a shared highway reference nor an advertised nearby amenity proves a fixed travel time, an accessible walking route or a suitable daily commute. Use the staff and client route guide to structure the comparison.

Keep serviced-office packages separate from conventional leases

If a ready-to-use format is relevant, include a specific serviced suite in the comparison. Midpoint's OnPoint serviced-office guide and serviced versus conventional comparison explain the different questions. Confirm inclusions and booking or credit rules for the selected package rather than assuming that the location determines them.

Turn the shortlist into viewings

Compare the live Midpoint office vacancies with the confirmed alternative proposals, then request the Midpoint plans, quote and viewing. Include your brief so the team can discuss actual suitable options.

If the brief also includes warehousing, keep 2 Kingfisher Avenue flagged: 3,849 m² in its numeric field conflicts with 3,300 m² in the description. Obtain approved figures before incorporating it into a combined proposal. Browse the Midpoint guides for related property decisions.

title: 6 Weaver Avenue: A Warehouse Listing Walkthrough
seoDescription: Read the published area, asking rate and specification statements for 6 Weaver Avenue. See what to confirm in plans, current photographs and a viewing.
excerpt: Understand 6 Weaver’s published building and yard figures, indicative base rent and the technical and occupation questions to resolve with leasing.
contentHtml:
The 6 Weaver Avenue warehouse listing at Midpoint brings together a warehouse, an office component and a separately described yard. This walkthrough explains the published figures and the questions to resolve before a viewing or quote. It is a review of the listing checked on 19 October 2026, not a report of a physical inspection or an approved engineering assessment.

Read it with the Midpoint warehouse leasing guide. The live vacancy page remains the place to check for updated information and request the current plans, photographs and availability.

Start with the area breakdown

The numeric listing field gives 11,443 m². Its description allocates 10,150 m² to warehousing and 1,293 m² to offices. Those two components add to 11,443 m²; the description separately records a 5,800 m² yard.

That arithmetic helps explain the listing, but it does not certify the measured rentable area or establish how the yard is charged. Request the approved area schedule and plan, identifying the building components, exclusive-use boundaries and the basis used in the quote. Do not add the yard to the building figure or assume that every described area is included at one rate.

The office component can then be tested against administration, meetings and staff requirements using the office-to-warehouse ratio guide. The published split does not prove that the existing layout suits a particular operation.

Read the asking rate with its limitations

The published asking rate is R109 per m² per month. Applied to the published 11,443 m², it gives R1,247,287 per month in indicative base rent. This is not an approved complete quote. Confirm VAT treatment, recoveries, utilities, parking, yard terms and any fit-out or service charges.

Use the warehouse occupation-cost guide to request the recurring and upfront costs on one consistent schedule.

Treat technical figures as verification points

The current description records 15 m height to eaves, a 3,000 kg/m² load-bearing figure and 2.5 MVA. These are published listing statements, not an independent confirmation of usable clearance, certified floor performance or power available to your equipment.

  • Height: request the relevant sections and check usable clearance below services and other obstructions for the proposed storage or equipment.
  • Floor: request the applicable load documentation and a suitable assessment for actual racking, point loads and equipment; a single area-load figure is not a full design assessment.
  • Power: confirm whether the figure concerns installed or proposed capacity, the supply and allocation to the unit, and the equipment supported by any backup arrangement.

The warehouse specification checklist and backup-power guide give a fuller viewing brief.

Separate existing arrangements from optional works

The description refers to an optional private entrance and design flexibility across the façade, entry points and internal layout. Ask which elements exist now, which are proposed, who would approve and fund changes, and what those changes mean for occupation timing.

For loading and circulation, request current entrance, door and yard drawings and assess the intended vehicles with the appropriate technical contacts. A published yard area alone cannot confirm turning space or a workable loading arrangement. Listing images may be illustrative or show proposed works; request current dated photographs and inspect the relevant areas.

Confirm dates and arrange a focused viewing

The availability field still states 1 September 2026 at this 19 October check. A past advertised date does not confirm readiness or that the premises remain unlet. Ask leasing for the current status, proposed handover date and dependencies.

Send your required warehouse and office functions, vehicle movements, equipment loads, budget and move date when you request a 6 Weaver viewing and source documents. Compare the other live warehouse opportunities and office-and-warehouse planning guide if your brief spans separate spaces.

2 Kingfisher Avenue remains flagged for its separate 3,849/3,300 m² area conflict; this walkthrough does not resolve it. Explore all Midpoint guides for more leasing decisions.
